newsitem.title: USA: Pinnacle Financial to acquire CB Bancorp.
newsitem.headline: Pinnacle Financial to acquire CB Bancorp.

text.p: Pinnacle Financial Services Inc. said Monday it agreed to purchase CB Bancorp Inc., another Midwestern banking company, in a stock deal worth about $41 million.
Under the agreement, Pinnacle will offer $35 worth of its stock for each of CB Bancorp's roughly 1.2 million shares outstanding.

If Pinnacle's average stock price exceeds $29 over a certain period, CB Bancorp shareholders will receive 1.2069 Pinnacle shares per CB Bancorp share. If Pinnacle's stock drops below $23, the ratio will go up to 1.5217, it said.
CB Bancorp's stock surged $4.75 to $33.375, while Pinnacle fell 50 cents to $27.25 on Nasdaq at mid-morning.
"This transaction allows us to fill the geographic gap between our Michigan and Indiana markets," said Richard Schanze, Pinnacle chief executive.
CB Bancorp, based in Michigan City, Ind., is the parent of Community Bank, with three offices in LaPorte County, Ind.
Pinnacle is the parent of Pinnacle Bank, based in St. Joseph, Mich., with 28 banking centres along the southern tip of Lake Michigan.
Pinnacle said it expects the deal to save costs and boost earnings per share and book value of the combined companies in the first year. One-time merger costs are expected to be minimal, it said.
The deal is expected to close in the second quarter, subject to regulatory and shareholder approvals.

Last November Pinnacle agreed to merge with Indiana Federal Corp., a bank holding company in northwest Indiana. Once completed, the two mergers would result in a $2.1 billion banking company with 50 banking centres located in northwestern Indiana and southwestern Michigan.
